edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a harmful direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.mechanism: Ethanol and acetaldehyde disrupt neuronal migration, synaptogenesis, and craniofacial development in the fetus, which is the core biology of fetal alcohol spectrum disorders.
edges.summary: The strongest piece here is the 2022 Bestry systematic review in Clin Epigenetics, which ties maternal alcohol use during pregnancy to fetal alcohol spectrum disorder in a direction that later studies largely support. That makes this edge more about calibrating magnitude and context than arguing over whether the signal exists at all.
edges.caveats: Residual confounding and reverse causation remain possible in some observational studies, so the main readout is direction and plausibility rather than one exact risk number.
